children: The Services PMI in Sweden fell to 55.7 in October 2026 from a downwardly revised 57.3 in September, marking its lowest reading in three months.
Still, the index remained above the average for the first ten months of the year for a third consecutive month.
The decline in the PMI was broad-based, with the new orders (56.1 vs. 58.8 in September) and delivery times (57.0 vs. 61.7) sub-indexes accounting for the largest declines.
The business activity index edged down to 57.1 from 57.5.
In contrast, the employment sub-index rose for the second month in a row (51.9 vs. 50.3).
Cost pressures remained elevated, with the suppliers’ input price index falling to 71.7 from 73.2 but staying well above its historical average of 58.5.
Meanwhile, the Composite PMI dropped to 57.0 from 57.7.
Jörgen Kennemar, responsible for the PMI analysis, said: “Growth in the private sector remains broad, with the stronger industrial economy offsetting the weaker development in the services sector.”

title: Sweden Services Sector Growth Cools in October
